text:
taylor: Quick Q on /rerank behaviour — how should we handle missing/null scores now that clients diverge? :thinking:
lia: Which divergence are you seeing? new clients omit scores, old ones send nulls?
 taylor: yep. Some backend tests show nulls used to be treated as -inf which pushed items to bottom, but a recent change to normalize/omit made them cluster with 0.0. Haven't audited why.
emma: historically we treated null as -inf to keep explicit scored items first. I think that was intentional for catalog sorts.
raj: We need a clear contract: two orthogonal concerns — (A) semantics for null/missing scores, (B) deterministic tie-breaking for equal scores.
 taylor: Agreed. Proposal sketch: keep legacy null-as--inf for backward compat; introduce optional `tie_break` param that selects the tie policy.
 raj: +1. Suggested `tie_break` enum: `stable_input` (deterministic based on input-order hash), `random:<seed>` (random but seedable), `positional` (keep input order). Default = `stable_input`.
 lia: If default changes we need a migration plan. Can we keep default behaviour identical to today for at least one release?
 emma: If current prod treats null as -inf, default should preserve that. We surface `tie_break` and a `null_score_policy` with values `minus_infty` or `treat_as_zero`. Default = `minus_infty` for backwards compat.
 taylor: Nice. Example request schema we can publish: 
```
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "inputs": ["q","doc1","doc2"],
  "scores": [0.82, null, 0.82],
  "tie_break": "stable_input", // stable_input | random:<seed> | positional
  "null_score_policy": "minus_infty", // minus_infty | treat_as_zero
  "stable_sort": true
}
```
 raj: Implementation notes: stable_input must be deterministic across languages and versions. We should pick a single hash function and salt, e.g. `xxhash64` with namespace `rerank-v1`. Add unit tests referencing canonical outputs.
 emma: We already use xxhash64 in other places — good for perf. Document exact byte encoding (UTF-8 normalize NFKC) so languages match.
 lia: Docs tasks: update OpenAPI, SDKs examples, migration guide mentioning legacy clients sending nulls. Runtime tasks: add param parsing, fallthrough logic, and a compatibility flag guard for canary.
 pr-bot: PR #4321 openschema: add `tie_break` & `null_score_policy` to rerank request schema (linked).
 taylor: Can we avoid a breaking change? Make params optional, default to preserve existing behaviour. Then roll out canary where `tie_break=stable_input` is opt-in first.
 raj: For canary: enable on Dedicated region X for a small % of traffic or by customer opt-in. We'll need tracing tags to correlate fallback/behavior.
 emma: Tests: unit tests for ordering with equal floats, with nulls, and fuzz test with 10k inputs to confirm stable sort doesn't regress perf.
 lia: I'll write the spec PR and SDK sample. Action items: lia -> spec + docs, raj -> runtime impl & canary plan, emma -> tests + cross-lang reference, taylor -> coordinate canary customers and release notes.
 taylor: Pinged the right people, thanks. Also want a short blurb for the changelog: "Add explicit tie-breaking and null-score policy to rerank; defaults preserve prior behaviour while enabling deterministic stable ordering options."
 emma: LGTM.
 taylor: @lia can you file the `changelog` entry and add a snippet to the breaking-changes page (even though it's non-breaking by default)?
 lia: Yep, will do.
 taylor: One last nit — random:<seed> should accept numeric seeds only to avoid parsing weirdness.
 raj: agreed. I'll enforce seed numeric regex and fallback error.
 taylor: Thanks all. Will follow up with example responses and a small sample log of ordering decisions for the canary. :thumbsup:
